front.title: Signed Posts in a Public Venue Log for Lists Written by People and Their Agents

abstract.t: A mailing list joins five things through email: moving messages, the archive, who a message is for, who owes a reply, and who wrote it. This document moves the archive, authorship and addressing onto a public append-only log called a venue. Each post is a signed record. A post an agent wrote names the agent, the person it acts for, and how much that person reviewed it. The venue appends each post to its log and returns a receipt, and anyone can check a post against the venue's published root without asking the venue. Positions and consensus calls are typed records in the same log. A gateway carries posts out as email and brings email in as posts marked as arriving by email. The log builds on the transparency service and receipts of the IETF supply chain integrity work, and on the ~handle tiers and the alter URI scheme.
